free_tier.stated: No free tier. The FAQ states 'The LokiProxy Premium Plan offers prices as low as $0.48/GB' and a trial by request: 'Yes, you can contact our online support to test our residential proxies.'
free_tier.notes: The trial is granted through a support chat on Telegram, so its size is unverified: behind a contact.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an address or a traffic quota, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable: a proxy session or a rented address, not stored bytes

egress.terms: Traffic-billed. 'No, it doesn't. Unlike the basic plan, the traffic purchased with the Premium Plan has no expiration date before allocation.' The Basic plan's traffic is valid 30 days and a high-purity line sells GB bundles valid 90 days.

interface_detail: HTTP(S) and SOCKS5; username and password for all products, an IP-allowlist ('API') method for rotating residential and unlimited products only; sticky sessions of 5 to 180 minutes or a new IP per request.
tooling: Any client that speaks an HTTP(S) or SOCKS5 proxy with a username and password or an allowlisted source address: curl -x, python requests, rclone --socks5, or a host-side hop for a runtime that cannot dial a proxy itself. The vendor also ships a client app for its short-term residential IPs.
chaining: A host-side hop dials the vendor's HTTP(S) or SOCKS5 endpoint with credentials; the upstream sees an address from the vendor's pool in place of the caller's address.

limits.value: Premium Plan from $0.48/GB with no expiry before allocation; Basic plan traffic valid 30 days; high-purity line bundles 5 GB $3.9/GB, 25 GB $2.5/GB, 500 GB $1.5/GB, 1 TB $1.2/GB, valid 90 days

limits_note: Pool claims on the home page: 35M+ residential IPs (rotating), 10M+ (high-purity line), 1,900+ IPv6 blocks as written ('1,900+ OCT unique IPs'). Static residential leases run up to 90 days. All are vendor claims, not measured.
binding_note: All lines are metered per GB or per IP lease; the expiry of purchased traffic differs by plan (none on Premium, 30 days on Basic).

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up form was not readable. The terms say registration 'requires you to provide us with your personal data via a dedicated form' and list failure to 'comply with our KYC requests' among grounds to suspend, so a KYC step may be asked; its trigger and documents are unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: The /pricing and /register paths returned no content to a page reader; the product page and terms are readable. unverified: payment methods, and the registration class of the exits (rung 5): no address was looked up.
confidence_note: Price and plan expiry are from the vendor's FAQ and price pages; identity detail is partial.
